findings.text: Decimal output helpers provide unsigned to decimal text conversion into a caller supplied buffer and return the position after the last digit. Large magnitudes are handled by splitting the input into smaller portions emitted as fixed size digit groups with propagation of excess, while smaller magnitudes use a direct truncation path; surplus leading zeros are removed so the result has no extra most significant zeros.

Bounded string formatting provides precision limited copy plus field width padding. Copying stops at terminator or precision limit while counting logical length, then short results are expanded with spaces either by shifting existing bytes right for right alignment or by appending spaces for left alignment. Physical writes are confined before an end marker while the returned pointer accounts for full logical extent.

Memory move provides overlap safe byte copy from a source range to a destination range and returns the destination. Direction is chosen from relative order of pointers so overlapping regions are preserved, and empty or coincident ranges have no effect beyond returning the destination.
String length provides a scan that counts bytes preceding the first zero byte, excluding the terminator itself.

Extended pointer formatting serves as the entry dispatcher for percent p conversions. It examines the following format character and transfers control to the renderer for the requested family, with a defined fallback to default pointer output when the character does not select a known extension.

Pointer pre validation provides uniform handling of unusable addresses before detailed formatting. Zero, very small numeric addresses and encoded error values cause a short diagnostic marker to be emitted through the bounded string path with a pointer sized default precision and a failure indication, while other values proceed to the selected renderer.

Error code naming provides translation of signed numeric failures to short symbolic labels. Selection uses magnitude to index a dense low table or an offset table near five hundred twelve plus one architecture specific value, with unknown magnitudes yielding absence; error pointer rendering uses the label when present and signed decimal otherwise.

Default pointer output provides privacy preserving hexadecimal rendering. Null and error values are shown directly, early boot debugging may substitute a non cryptographic hash derived value, otherwise a stable hashed identifier is shown; when identifier generation fails a fixed placeholder is emitted. Default width follows pointer size with zero padding and lowercase digits.

Restricted pointer output provides a global policy with three behaviors: default hashed rendering, conditional disclosure only outside hard interrupt soft interrupt and non maskable contexts when the caller has syslog privilege with unchanged user and group identity, and unconditional suppression. Suppressed values render as null.

Bounded renderers preserve the invariant that no byte is stored at or beyond the end marker, while the returned position always reflects full logical length including bytes that did not fit and padding that was requested. Rightward shifting clamps the moved portion to available room and fills vacated prefix with spaces.

Decimal grouping preserves the invariant that least significant groups are emitted first with excess carried to more significant groups, and that only the most significant group is stripped of leading zeros. A zero overall quotient leaves a single zero rather than empty output.

Format control observed across renderers carries field width for padding or element count, precision for string limits with negative one meaning unbounded, flag bits for left alignment zero padding sign and digit style, and a numeric base for radix selection. Width and precision interact with bounded output to determine logical length independently of truncation.

Dentry name rendering holds read side RCU protection for the entire traversal from target through parents and for copying name bytes, releasing on all exits including early validation failure. This keeps parent links and name storage stable across the critical section.

Filesystem and block renderers provide path and device naming. Dentry rendering emits a selectable suffix of one to four trailing components with separator handling and precision bounded output; file rendering unwraps to the embedded path dentry; block rendering emits the disk name plus partition number with an extra separator when the disk name ends in a digit.

Symbol rendering provides address to name translation with mode selection by leading and trailing format characters, covering backtrace, plain symbol with or without offset and build identifier variants plus return address adjustment. When symbol support is unavailable the contract degrades to zero padded hexadecimal with radix prefix.

Binary dump rendering provides byte array and bit set output. Byte arrays emit two digits per element with selectable separator and a capped count; bit sets emit either most significant first hexadecimal chunks separated by commas or merged decimal ranges for contiguous set bits, each honoring the requested bit count.

Link address rendering provides six byte address output with case reversal and separator variants selected by trailing modifiers, covering colon dash contiguous reversed and upper case forms. Output is staged as a short terminated temporary and then emitted through the bounded string path.

Network address rendering provides Internet protocol version four and six output including full, compressed and socket decorated forms. Version four supports leading zero and byte order variants; version six supports longest zero run compression with special handling for mapped addresses; socket forms optionally add bracketed port flow and scope decorations. Unrecognized families or specifiers produce a short invalid marker.

Pointer extension selection behaves as a shallow decision machine where the first extension character chooses a family and, for families with styles, one or two further characters refine separator, order, case, compression or decoration before delegation. Each path terminates in exactly one delegated renderer and returns its updated position.

Hazards center on silent truncation, logical versus physical length confusion, and wide stores. Callers must treat the returned position as required length rather than a writable address when truncation occurred; shift and pad paths may report more than fits; pair digit emission uses wide unaligned stores that assume architecture tolerance.
Invalid address markers are fixed texts "(null)" for zero input and "(efault)" for low or encoded error addresses.
Pointer identity placeholders are fixed texts "(____ptrval____)" for eight byte pointers and "(ptrval)" otherwise, with restricted atomic context failure using fixed text "pK-error".
Invalid extension markers are fixed texts "(einval)" for unsupported sub specifiers, "(%pI?)" and "(%pi?)" for unknown network specifier case, and "(%pA?)" for unsupported Rust formatter use.
Special hexadecimal control uses base sixteen with special small and zero pad attributes, precision negative one, and width two plus twice the byte size to cover prefix and digits.
